text: Việt Nam eyes accurate, real-time national land database in digitalisation push

HÀ NỘI - Efforts to build a national land database are gathering pace, with more than 55.65 million land plots meeting the 'accurate, complete, clean and live' data standards by the end of October 2026.
However, ensuring that information remains up to date, interconnected and accessible for effective use remains a major challenge.
The Ministry of Agriculture and Environment reported that there are nearly 105.2 million land plots nationwide as of late October.
More than 70.3 million plots, or 66.8 per cent of the total, had been incorporated into the land database.
Of these, more than 55.65 million met the required data standards, while nearly 14.65 million had records that still required additional information or verification.
Almost 34.9 million plots had yet to be included in the database.
Around 43.17 million plots had been synchronised with the National Data Centre.
The figures highlight significant progress in digitalisation, but also reveal the gap between simply having digital records and ensuring that the information can be reliably used.

The digital transformation of land management is also aligned with Politburo's Resolution 57 on breakthroughs in science and technology, innovation and digital transformation, which identifies digital infrastructure and data exploitation as important drivers of national development.
Mai Văn Phấn, deputy director of the Department of Land Administration, said land data could not be cleaned up through a one-off campaign but required regular updates whenever changes occurred.
Without timely adjustments, the database risked becoming outdated, potentially affecting land users' rights and the effectiveness of State management, he said.
In the final months of 2026, priority would be given to the completion and verification of existing records that do not yet meet required standards.
In 2027, the focus would be on surveying land, preparing cadastral maps and building databases for areas where information remains unavailable.

During recent National Assembly's discussions on amendments to the Law on Land, Deputy Tạ Đình Thi from Hà Nội said land data should not be regarded simply as administrative information but a special resource associated with space, time, value and property rights.
He proposed establishing the national land database as an official source of information to pave the way for transactions and administrative procedures to be conducted through digital platforms.
Another important requirement is a transparent mechanism for handling inaccurate records.

Citizens need to know which agency is responsible for verification and correction, how long the process will take and how their rights will be protected if errors affect land transfers, mortgages or other land-use rights.
Beyond public administration, the land database development also plays significant role in the development of businesses and the real estate market as well as the operation of the banking system.

Nguyễn Văn Khôi, chairman of the Vietnam Real Estate Association, said when digitised, regularly updated and appropriately disclosed, the land data will help businesses access the market while enabling authorities to determine land prices and monitor market more effectively.

However, as land records are closely linked to property rights and personal information, it is necessary to clearly define which data can be disclosed, who is entitled to access it and the purposes for which it can be used, alongside appropriate requirements for cybersecurity and information protection.

As Việt Nam advances the implementation of Resolution 57, the ability to maintain, connect and effectively exploit reliable land data will be crucial to translating digital transformation targets into tangible economic and social benefits. - VNS
